steps.decide: Whether the whole card is a link or only its title, and the keyboard model that follows
The one piece of information that makes a card scannable in a list
Media weight and its ratio at 390px
Hover and focus treatment that still works on touch

rules.statement: A card has exactly one activation target; nested interactive children either leave the card or the card stops being clickable.
Every card in a list exposes the same anchor (title, price, date) in the same position so scanning works without reading.
Media keeps a fixed aspect ratio per list; mixed ratios break comparison and cause layout shift.
Hover is never the only affordance: focus is styled at least as clearly and touch receives the same information without hover.

motion.reducedMotion: instant elevation change, no information carried by the shadow

motion.noneReason: activation replaces the view; a press animation delays it
the next document or the restored card is already at its default state

refused.reason: a static card is not a control and does not react to pointer

sections.intent: Make one record scannable and comparable inside a list without hiding what distinguishes it.
nicheDifferences: Commerce cards need price and availability
Editorial cards need date and reading time
Operate cards replace table rows on narrow screens
styling: Text truncation stated (lines) rather than incidental
a11y: No nested interactive children inside a clickable card
Focus ring visible on the card or its single link
responsive: Columns reduce until one; card order stays the same
Truncation never hides the anchor field
Touch target is the whole card or the whole link
copy: Anchor wording consistent across the list
Truncation keeps the distinguishing words first
alternatives: A definition list is better than cards for two fields
A table is better when more than four fields are compared
acceptance: Every card exposes the same anchor in the same position
Keyboard reaches each card's single target
failureCases: Card click plus inner link producing two navigations
